content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Construct genetic diagrams to show inheritance patterns
Use correct format and notation for genetic diagrams
Interpret genetic diagrams to determine offspring ratios
Apply genetic diagrams to various inheritance problems

is a formal way of showing how alleles are passed from parents to offspring. While Punnett squares show possible combinations, genetic diagrams provide a more complete picture including parental phenotypes, genotypes, gametes, and offspring. Learning to draw these correctly is essential for genetics questions.
A complete genetic diagram should include:
In mice, brown fur (B) is dominant to white fur (b). Draw a genetic diagram for a cross between two heterozygous brown mice.
Parental phenotypes: Brown mouse × Brown mouse
A brown mouse could be BB or Bb. Describe how you would determine its genotype using a test cross, and show both possible outcomes.
Cross the brown mouse with a white mouse (bb).
Outcome 1: If the brown mouse is BB
Parental phenotypes: Brown mouse × White mouse
Conclusion: If all offspring are brown, parent was BB
Outcome 2: If the brown mouse is Bb
Parental phenotypes: Brown mouse × White mouse
Conclusion: If some offspring are white, parent was Bb
Two tall pea plants are crossed. Of the offspring, 75% are tall and 25% are short. Determine the parental genotypes. (T = tall, t = short)
A 3:1 ratio indicates Tt × Tt cross
Step 2: Draw the genetic diagram to confirm
This confirms the 3:1 ratio, so parents are both Tt

Albinism is controlled by a recessive allele (a). Two parents with normal pigmentation have a child with albinism. 
a) What are the parents' genotypes?
b) What is the probability their next child will have albinism?
a) The child has albinism (aa), so must have inherited 'a' from both parents. Since parents appear normal, they must be carriers (Aa).
